title: Packaging
explain: A virtual environment keeps each project's libraries separate so versions never clash. Create one with `python -m venv .venv`, activate it, then install with `pip install`. Save your dependencies in `requirements.txt` so anyone can recreate the setup.
code:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install requests
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pip install -r requirements.txt  # on another machine
exercise: Create a virtual environment in a new folder, install `rich`, and write the dependency list to `requirements.txt`.
tip: Don't install packages globally for every project. Without a virtual environment, one project's upgrade can break another.
